(i) the accuracy of DIC measurements of small-magnitude (< 0.1%) strain fields is limited by the noise-signal level of the images, (ii) optimal parameters for image processing can be determined experimentally based on the single-image noise level, (iii) the intra- and the inter-specimen repeaterability of DIC is lower than strain gauge measurements, (iv) DIC overestimates E and ν by 1.9% and 3%, respectively, and

(i) the accuracy of DIC measurements of small-magnitude strain is affected by the image processing parameters; (ii) the accuracy is further affected by the noise level in the images, which can be minimized by image pre-selection; (iii) the accuracy of strain measurements can be improved by optimizing the parameters and pre-selecting images, although the repeatability is not improved; (iv) the trueness of strain measurements is improved by optimizing the image processing parameters and pre-selective images
